notes.title: Small update
notes.notes:
Greetings Shoppers!

This foggy night's update includes a handful of bug fixes, some new products from Ellie around the store, and some updates to the mannequin's behavior.  I completely changed the way her movement is processed, but in theory shoppers shouldn't really see too much of a difference.  We did make her move a little slower, hopefully prevented her occasional cheating, and added another option to her repertoire.  Hopefully this makes the blessed difficulty a little easier for people to explore in.  If you run into issues or its not behaving the way you expect, please let us know.

There are a few other minor changes as we try and focus the rest of our efforts on getting the main story of the game completed.  Short of major bugs or problems we're going to be focusing on getting all the things done we need for our (hopefully) August release schedule.  The new areas are coming along quite well and we're looking forward to getting [strike]meat processing to full capacity[/strike] areas open to explore.

Safe shopping out there, we'll see you in the mist.

notes.title: Mechanics update
notes.notes:
Greetings Shoppers,

Today we're bringing you an update with a few changes that should significantly change the difference between the Blessed and Nameless difficulties.  Namely, the Ellpad will offer extra help for avatars in Blessed mode - the Ellnotes tell you whats next on your shopping list, and may offer help for other tasks as well.  Additionally, for those who find themselves lost in endless places, the Ellpad can give you a guiding line to where you're trying to go.

There are also some new things to interact with in the store, as well as things that may occur while shopping.

Finally, we implemented more bug fixes and corrected a few obscure items on the shopping list and made sure they should count towards lists correctly.

We have another update with a few more features and a few more bugs to fix coming soon, and I'm working on a big push to get a lot of the dialogue finished.  We have some new and exciting, awesome people who have offered to do voice acting for us, so we'll have more information on that soon!

Happy shopping!  We'll see you in the mist...

notes.title: Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
Greetings Shoppers.  We have our first big update of the month tonight.  There's a huge list of bug fixes included in this update.  It's a wide range of bugs, from game breaking to trivial.

We believe we've addressed almost all the bugs that were reported or we saw while people were playing the demo.  We've also gone through and triple checked the products so that they should be marked correctly and should be properly interactable.  The one exception is the grab and go sections of the store.  You should be able to currently take things successfully, but it can cause some issues in the foods there.  In our next update this month, players will use the grab'n'go containers to acquire the pre-cooked foods which should resolve those issues.

If we've missed something, please let us know!

Stay tuned for our next update, around the end of this month, which will bring some new features, QoL updates and the revamped difficulty system amongst other things.

As always, stay safe.  See you in the mist.

notes.title: Devblog #6 - The one in which an important lesson is learned.
notes.notes:
Greetings shoppers.  I realize it's been a bit since we had a status update, so let's catch up..

The Demo came out, and has had a fantastic welcoming.  Many, many thanks to everyone who has downloaded it and given it a try.  We're almost giddy with how much everyone has enjoyed playing it and experiencing the world we've put together.  Thank you all for your feedback, patience with bugs, constructive criticism and kind words.  We've strived to address as many of your issues as we can and have had amazing feedback that has changed the shape of the game.  We've actually overhauled the difficulty system - the new system will be more like a "Lore and Explore" (Blessed) mode vs an "Advanced" (Nameless) mode that is as we intended.  Blessed difficulty will still have deaths and hazards, but things like the murderousness of our store inhabitants will be decreased, and instead alternative punishments will occur.  We're also adding a few features to make getting used to the store easier in Blessed difficulty based on your feedback, but expect you to be more capable for Nameless difficulty.

We hope that this gives people who want a little breathing room to experience the world, read the backs of items, and explore more of the lore to be able to do so, while those desiring to experience the full perils of Last Chance Market to have a worthy challenge.  There will also be some slight differences in story and outcome, so we hope you'll give Nameless a try after experiencing Blessed.

Unfortunately, this update isn't all good news.  At the end of October we took a week off because we'd been burning the candle at both ends nonstop, and shortly after we came back I made a hubris-inspired mistake.

For anyone who isn't interested in technical details, I recommend skipping ahead to the TL;DR.  

Essentially, the new version of Unreal Engine, 5.5, has a new system of lighting, Megalights, that should've purportedly increased performance of our lighting.  For anyone keeping score at home, all our lighting is done dynamically, no baking or Global Illumination, so performance has always been a bugaboo of ours.  Thus, of course, it was with excitement that I downloaded and updated our project (after backing it up of course) and started fiddling.  Surprisingly Megalights actually tanked performance, BUT improvements in the general lighting system in 5.5 actually gave us a 20-25% increase in fps in our heavy load situations, which is crazy and I was happy to take as a gain.  Caveat emptor.

Because of the work we were doing on the game, it wasn't until a month later that I realized that 5.5 also introduced a bug that prevented us from editing something called Instanced meshes.  Now, Instanced meshes are essentially a way of grouping and rendering similar objects so that they're more performant.  And because of the sheer volume of products we offer in the store, almost all of them are some form of instanced mesh.  Not being able to edit them is somewhere between disastrous and apocalyptic.  However, after a lot of hemming and hawing, we decided that rather than lose invested dev time, we would continue working on other things tangentially while we waited for Epic to push a fix.  Fast forward to last week, and the latest hotfix for UE has come out, and there's still no fix in sight.  It's been two and a half months that this bug has been hindering us and we simply had to do something.  So, with a heavy heart, we decided to revert to our UE5.4 backup and re-implement the work we've done since mid-November.  It means doing some things over again tediously, but some things like source code updates should be minimal to fix. It was, however, the only real avenue in order to continue working on the game.

TL;DR Adopting new technology set us back ~2 months in dev time.  Fortunately, it shouldn't be a 1:1 ratio to get back to where we were, but it still delays everything.

So looking forward, what this means is that we're hoping to prioritize the demo fixes and then updates this month, get those out, then continue pushing forward and finishing setting up the world and the story within.  Being a two person team, and our first game, this whole project is a learning experience and unfortunately this lesson is a harsh one.  But we appreciate everyone's patience and understanding, you have all been the greatest inspiration to stick with it and keep going, so we truly thank you.

Expect another message this month as updates get pushed.

See you all in the mist.

notes.title: Demo out now!
notes.notes:
We're happy to announce that we've released a demo as part of Steam's NextFest and Spooktober events!

The game is very much incomplete early-access, as such the demo is limited in areas, monsters, and game play elements, restricting how far you can progress.  However, we wanted to give shoppers the opportunity to explore the store, view some of the lore and take in the atmosphere here at Last Chance Market.  Shoppers will be provided with a questionnaire at the end of their shopping experience, and any constructive feedback would be most welcome!

Of course, the trickster god is working against us, so we've run into a slew of bugs and problems right out of the gate.  That being said, we are existing purely on caffeine, adrenaline and pain at this point, working sleeplessly to fix bugs that we find patch holes in the fabric of existence.

Now that we have a playable experience released into the mist, we'll be making much more regular updates here and on our discord as we push regular updates.  Expect a manic flurry of demo updates over the next two weeks until Halloween, then hopefully settling down to a regular bi-weekly rhythm after that.

As always, find us in the mist at our lighthouse on discord, and wishlist now for more updates in the near future!

Good luck out there.

notes.title: Devblog #5 - The Last Leg of the Journey
notes.notes:
Another season, another brief update my fellow mist-dwellers.  The work continues unabated on opening the store for business.  New challenges continue to rear their heads, but they are steadily overcome.  We have restructured our release schedule somewhat, and are planning on releasing a demo and early access shortly afterward.  And while I abhor giving timelines, as they have repeatedly shown me to be overly optimistic, I do feel obliged to say that I feel confident that both should be out before the end of the year, if not before Halloween itself.

One of the continual challenges has been using the latest version of Unreal Engine.  The urge to use the shiny new features of each update is always offset by the learning curve and adjustments to existing code that are required.  However, as of this latest version, 5.4, I've been able to figure out some issues.  Unfortunately we're hitting some limitations on the engine itself, but we're expanding our menu options so that people with varying hardware can utilize as much as their systems will allow.

Gameplay-wise, we've added a few big, memorable things lately which I refuse to speak of because of spoilers.  Needless to say, I'm super excited to share our work with you.  We both feel you'll all love it.

Do you hear that?  The foghorn's blaring again, which means I'm back to the code-stone.  As always, you can find us on Discord should you have any questions, comments, or just feel like talking about horror. 

Stay tuned, we'll be back shortly.

notes.title: Devblog #4 - The Long Road
notes.notes:
The seasons change but our work continues.  We've got a short teaser to share with everyone today, inspired by working with the things that inhabit the store.

[previewyoutube=AnSYQb91y2w;full][/previewyoutube]

Just a taste to wet the palate.

While the project has certainly taken longer than we've hoped, we've been consistently chugging away at making somethin that we're proud of and hope everyone will enjoy,  For a two person team making their first real game, its been a long road, but we can see the store lights shining in the distance through the fog.  Every once in a while the terrain shifts when we hit technical hurdles or decide to rewrite part of the story, but the journey continues unabated.

Just as a bit of news that we're excited about, we've gone back and changed our dialogue system in the hope of providing language localization as soon as possible.  Combined with regional pricing, we're hoping to reach as many new potential [strike]flesh slabs[/strike] [b]customers [/b]as possible.

As always, if you have any questions about the game, would like to check out progress, or just want to chat about anything horror, feel free to stop by our discord. We'll be lurking in the dark.

Stay safe out there.

notes.title: Devblog #3 - Delayed by the fog
notes.notes:
Hello Last Chance Market shoppers, we just wanted to make a quick update.  While we've been waylaid by various issues (disease, computer malfunctions, and the ever continuing cycle of trying to update unreal engine), we have never stopped work on getting the store ready for your resumed patronage.

Honestly, every time we try to estimate how long things will take, we seem to be wrong and its a repetitive blow to morale.  So we're simply not going to make guesses.

That being said, what we've been working on lately is a pretty long list.  We've added a new area to the store with new lore to find.  The menu system has gotten a revamp and been completely fleshed out.  Plus we've been working on an intro sequence to introduce players to the game and the few mechanics that we employ.

As a part of all that, one of our biggest concerns is always the number and difficulty of puzzles.  Your feedback on that is the main reason we're looking forward to early access and getting the community involved.  Our natural inclination as gamers ourselves is to make it as challenging as possible because thats the kind of game we love.  But we also want to tell an intriguing story that's accessible for everyone, so we've decided to make two difficulty levels for players to choose from.  Both difficulties will have the same puzzles and content, but Ellie may be a bit more helpful on the easier difficulty, as well as some forms of progress being maintained.  The second difficulty will be more challenging and engage the player more in the stealth mechanics, requiring you to survive in order to succeed.

Last but not least, we've written a bit of a backstory to the whole... situation at Last Chance Market.  A bit of a prelude to the events if you will.  We're going to be polishing that up a little and then releasing it into the void on various creepypasta homes, and maybe even sending it to a couple of our favorite narrators on youtube to see if they're interested.

Overall we're very excited about the progress we're making and quite excited to share with everyone, hopefully Soon(TM).  This has really been a project we're pouring ourselves into and we have big plans on how to continue the story and the experience well after this first game is released.

As always, if you have any questions about the game, would like to know how its going, or just want to chat about eldritch things in the dark, feel free to stop by our discord.  We're always lurking.

Stay safe friends, see you in the mist.

notes.title: Devblog #2
notes.notes:
Greetings programs.

Lost Harbinger here with another signal from the mists.  It's been a busy couple of weeks here in the lighthouse, mostly focused on story and audio.

In game text is always a tricky problem to address.  We know our fellow gamers, so we know how often people will just skip through walls of text, regardless of how much we, as the developers, want them to read the rich story we've written.  So one of the things we've always wanted was voice acting for everything that we really wanted conveyed.  But with an indie budget, that's not always realistic, so we've been coming up with creative ways to put a voice to everything we can.

Fortunately, one of our main characters we can use text-to-speech as they are, in fact, an artificial intelligence.  The "Emotive Listening & Learning Pad", or Ellpad, is Last Chance Market's new shopping assistant, featuring the store's mascot, Ellie the Elk!  Through the Ellpad, Ellie will be able to assist shoppers in finding items throughout the store.  Ellie can also interact more directly with shoppers, giving them detailed information on the store's displays and might even give hints on how to [strike]survive[/strike] find the best deals!

We've also been working hard on getting the sound design itself [i]just right[/i].  Sound design is undoubtedly one of the most important aspects of a horror game, but we didn't want to limit ourselves to the usual drones and atmospheric sounds.  Because what grocery store doesn't have music playing in the background?  So we're very happily adding a variety of creative commons-friendly music to the store's PA system.  Quite a bit of the music is from the amazing Karl Casey @ White Bat Audio, who we've been listening to on youtube for years now.  If you haven't heard of him, he's got some amazing dark synth and cyberpunk mixes that make for great background listening, we highly recommend checking him out.

That's going to be it for now, just a quick update before returning to deciphering the code.  Stay tuned for more signals from the fog.

notes.title: Devblog #1
notes.notes:
Greetings programs.

Lost Harbinger here, broadcasting from the foggy coastal town of Last Chance, with the first of our Last Chance Market dev blogs.  While I tend to want to work on making the game, rather than writing about it, now that we're getting [i]very [/i]close to releasing Early Access I thought I'd go ahead and start making some regular (weekly/biweekly) posts to keep up to date on how development is going, what we have planned and gather community feedback.

First off, I want to address our planned release date for Early Access.  Obviously our anticipated timeline was inaccurate.  This is our first game, and there are a fair number of pitfalls in indie game development, not the least of which is underestimation of time required, and the possibility that, with only two people involved, work can be derailed by real life events.  Unfortunately, this winter has been plagued with literal plague and other non-digital complications that prevented us from making progress the way we had desired.  When we did get back to the bottomless pit that is gamedev, we ran into other hurdles, like an overeager upgrade to Unreal Engine 5.1 which concluded with a week of hair-pulling-out and a reversion to Unreal Engine 5.0.3.

But, back at it we are, and closer than ever to [strike]feeding...[/strike] errr... [b]satisfying [/b]the customers of Last Chance Market.  In fact, I'm happy to say that earlier this week we did some optimization testing to check performance on a range of systems and were extremely pleased with the results.

Performance has been a bit of a gremlin for us for a few reasons.  For one, in doing our best to create a detailed environment, the game routinely has ~6,000 unique actors loaded in a fairly small area, many of which are instanced meshes, meaning they are drawn anywhere from two to two hundred times (For example, one actor consists of say, 30 boxes of cereal on the shelf, or 100 oranges lined up in produce).

Additionally, light and illumination are a huge part of the ambience we're trying so hard to build.  So the decision was made early on (hubris or brilliance?) to use only dynamic lighting.  That means none of the lights or shadows are pre-baked, and can be altered in real-time, including subject to gravity and whatever creatures might bump into them.  Combining that with Unreal Engine 5.0's new Virtual Shadow Map system, we've been able to build a world that both looks amazingly foreboding, while being very reactive.

Which is why, over the previous week, I've been working on an extensive update to our lighting system, adding some nifty new effects and increasing performance.  The result is that even low to mid-tier graphics cards were able to run the game on high quality settings while maintaining ~35-50+ average fps.

Meanwhile, the saner half of our dev duo, Onyx, has been hard at work putting the finishing touches on the bathroom mirrors.  I don't want to spoil the surprise, but her work will put new meaning into the phrase "Stare into the abyss and the abyss stares back".  I'm very excited.

Finally, I'm hesitant to say when exactly early access will be out because it seems to tempt the elder things in dimensions just beyond human perception to interfere, but I feel confident that if we can continue our work here at the lighthouse, the market will be accepting customers by the end of March.

Stay tuned for more signals from the fog.

notes.title: Last Chance Market Opening Update
notes.notes:
[h1]Attention[/h1]
[h2]Last Chance Residents & Market Shoppers[/h2]

It is with a heavy heart that I am writing to inform you that the opening of the Market will be delayed.  While I had hoped to have the repairs completed by the end of Elktober, I must admit the damage from the electrical fire earlier this summer, which claimed the lives of two people, was far more extensive than I had originally estimated.  With staff shortages limiting us to two full time employees, earthquake related road closures and regular power grid disruptions due to the ongoing solar flare activity, we have simply been unable to complete the work on our expected schedule.  My commitment is to the best shopping experience possible, and with that in mind I now expect us to be ready for shoppers in the second half of November.  In the meantime, we will be conituing our weekend Farmer's Market style sales in the parking lot until the store opens again.

On the bright side, we've taken this opportunity to update the store with some exciting new features.  Our new technology, featuring the deimOS AI system, is ready to make your visit to Last Chance Market better than ever.  We have a new interactive shopping assistant, the Ellpad, to help you quickly hunt down your shopping lists.  Swing by our new recipe kiosk to find delicious recipes featuring our sales of the day.  Or utilize the new self checkout to avoid waiting in line!

I do want to mention that we are still inviting participants in the annual Elktober FunHunt to park in our lot, conveniently located across from the starting point at Leng Forest Visitor Center.  We will have paintball supplies for those coming as Hunters as well as locally made, lightweight antlers for those participating as Elk.  Additionally, we will have GPS, maps and bear spray on sale for everyone involved.  A record number of forest search and rescues had to be made this year, be sure you FunHunt safely and responsibly!

Lastly, I want to give a big shout out to the Last Chance Secondary School's hockey team for the amazing fundraiser they had in the parking lot last week.  The community support was amazing and will allow them to get all the equipment they need this year.  Big thanks to everyone involved.  GO TSUNAMIS!

Looking forward to seeing you soon,
Tom Douglas
Last Chance Market Proprietor 

[i]Transcribed from the Leng Tribune weekend insert.[/i]
